references.text: The Levites were brought forward to stand before the Lord and serve him, as described in Deuteronomy 18:7.
The service of the Levites for the God of Israel and their position among the people parallels the service in the name of the Lord.
Aaron and his sons were chosen for priestly service to the Lord, a service in which the Levites also participated.
The Levites were to perform the service at the tent of meeting, which is the same service in the name of the Lord.
The tribe of Levi was set apart to carry the ark of the covenant of the Lord, to stand before the face of the Lord and serve him, and to bless in his name.
The priest who stands and serves for the Lord your God is a direct parallel to the service of the Levites.
Aaron's sons were set apart to consecrate the Most Holy Place and offer incense before the face of the Lord, to serve him and to bless in his name.
Every priest stands day after day performing his service, which reflects the daily service of the Levites for the Lord.
